config.title: useDeferredValue

intro.title: useDeferredValue
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a searchable product list that updates in real-time as you type, but with a smooth user experience where the search input remains responsive even during heavy filtering. You'll learn how to use the React hook useDeferredValue to defer updating a computationally expensive part of the UI, like a large list of search results, while keeping the rest of the interface snappy. The main technologies involved are React, JavaScript (JSX), and the built-in useDeferredValue hook for managing performance. By the end, you'll understand how to apply this hook to optimize rendering and prevent lag in interactive applications.
intro.usecase: The useDeferredValue hook is essential for building responsive interfaces that handle expensive re-renders, such as large data dashboards with real-time filters. For example, in an analytics dashboard where users can type to filter a massive dataset, you can defer the expensive filtering computation to keep the input field snappy and responsive. This pattern is also crucial in search interfaces with live previews, complex form validations, or any UI where immediate user feedback is prioritized over background updates.

objectives: Implement useDeferredValue to defer state updates for non-urgent UI rendering
Configure a deferred value to improve performance during rapid input changes
Integrate useDeferredValue with input components to manage user interactions
Render deferred values alongside regular state values in React components
Manipulate component rendering priorities using deferred value patterns
Construct a search interface that utilizes deferred values for filtering operations
Control UI responsiveness by applying deferred updates to computationally expensive operations

steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in all three from 'react'.

steps.title: Initialize search input state
steps.instruction: Inside your component, use useState to create a state variable named 'searchTerm' with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty string and destructure the returned array into searchTerm and setSearchTerm.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for a text input
const [text, setText] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a searchTerm state variable ready to track user input.
successCriteria: searchTerm state is declared using useState with an empty string initial value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty string initial value and naming the variable 'searchTerm'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Use useState to create a state variable named 'searchTerm' initialized to an empty string.

steps.title: Create deferred search value
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, use the useDeferredValue hook to create a deferred version of the searchTerm state variable. Name this deferred variable 'deferredSearchTerm'.
steps.hint: Call useDeferredValue with the searchTerm state variable as its argument, and assign the result to a new constant.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating a deferred value
const deferredInput = useDeferredValue(inputValue);
steps.expectedOutcome: A deferred version of the searchTerm state is created using useDeferredValue, ready to be used in the UI.
successCriteria: The useDeferredValue hook is called with searchTerm and assigned to a constant named deferredSearchTerm.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're calling useDeferredValue with searchTerm and storing the result in a constant named deferredSearchTerm.
steps.feedbackWrong: The deferred value wasn't created correctly. Remember to call useDeferredValue(searchTerm) and assign it to deferredSearchTerm.

steps.title: Define input change handler
steps.instruction: Inside your component, define a function named 'handleSearchChange' that takes an event parameter and updates the 'searchTerm' state with the input's value.
steps.hint: The function should use the 'setSearchTerm' setter with 'event.target.value'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'handleSearchChange' that updates the searchTerm state when called with an input event.
successCriteria: The component contains a function named 'handleSearchChange' that calls 'setSearchTerm(event.target.value)'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named 'handleSearchChange' and updates 'searchTerm' with 'event.target.value'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler function is missing or incorrect. Define a function named 'handleSearchChange' that updates 'searchTerm' with the input value.

steps.title: Add search input field
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add an input element with type='text', value bound to the searchTerm state variable, and an onChange handler that calls handleSearchChange.
steps.hint: Remember to use JSX syntax for the input element. The value attribute should be set to {searchTerm} and onChange should be {handleSearchChange}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: input element with state binding
<input type="text" value={inputValue} onChange={handleChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now includes a text input field that will display and update the searchTerm state.
successCriteria: An input element with type='text', value={searchTerm}, and onChange={handleSearchChange} is added to the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your input element has all three required attributes: type='text', value={searchTerm}, and onChange={handleSearchChange}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or incomplete. Check that you've added it to the return statement with the correct attributes.

steps.expectedOutcome: The filterItems function is defined and ready to be used with the deferred search value.
successCriteria: A function named filterItems is defined, takes a search term parameter, includes an artificial delay loop, and returns filtered results.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function includes an artificial delay loop and returns filtered results.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to create a function named filterItems that takes a search term and returns filtered results with an artificial delay.

steps.title: Display filtered results using deferred value
steps.instruction: In your component's return statement, call the filterItems function with deferredSearchTerm and map the results to display them as list items inside an unordered list.
steps.hint: Use the filterItems function you created earlier, passing deferredSearchTerm as the argument. Then use .map() on the returned array to create <li> elements for each item.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a list of filtered items below the search input, using the deferred search term for filtering.
successCriteria: The filterItems function is called with deferredSearchTerm, and the results are mapped to <li> elements inside a <ul>.
